fields.meta_description: Build a copywriter landing page that turns readers into briefs. Four examples: a free teardown, a per-email quote, a case study, a retainer form.
fields.h1: Build a Copywriter Landing Page That Brings in Paid Briefs
fields.hero_description: Build a copywriter landing page that shows your best work, quotes a price, and saves each inquiry to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts on a Copywriter's Page
fields.features_subheading: Describe your niche, your offer, and the work you are proudest of, and Emergent builds the page and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
A positioning line drafted from your notes

Paste your bio, your niche, and two client results, and Emergent drafts the headline and the sections under it. Mark up any line by prompt, as you would a client's draft.
fields.feature_2:
Samples shown with the result they got

Add each writing sample as a card with its format, the client, and the number it moved, such as a welcome email's open rate. Prospects read the proof before your prices.
fields.feature_3:
A quote the visitor works out alone

Set a price per email or per page, and the page adds up a quote as the visitor picks what they need. The total is saved with the request, so your reply starts from it.
fields.feature_4:
Inquiries saved as rows you own

Each inquiry lands in a database you own, with the project type, the deadline, and the section the visitor came from. Sort by deadline and answer the closest one first.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a big project comes in

Name the answer that matters, such as a monthly retainer, and the app sends you a Slack message or an email on a match. Smaller requests wait in the table for your reply.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, or your code on GitHub

Publish on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export of the page and its table to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Of 31 free teardowns in October, 8 became paid rewrites

Ismay Varnham rewrites one headline for free, page by page. Her form asks for the page URL and the one action that page should drive, and the app emails her each request. October brought 31 requests. Owners of 8 of those pages then paid for a full rewrite, and each one is marked in her table.
fields.tab_content_2:
The founder picks 6 emails and sees $1,650 on the page

Agnes Mereweather charges by the email: $275 for each one in a launch sequence. A founder who picks 6 emails watches the quote reach $1,650 before pressing send. Her table keeps every request with the email count, the total, and the founder's launch date.
fields.tab_content_3:
Before the rewrite, 140 trial signups; after it, 231

Merrit Pellingham's best proof is one headline. Her case study sets the old and new headline of the Steepwell Tea subscription page side by side, with the client's numbers under each: 140 trial signups in the 30 days before the rewrite, 231 in the 30 days after. A request form sits under the numbers.
fields.tab_content_4:
Brands sending 8 or more emails a month reach Rollo in Slack

Rollo Brackley's inquiry form asks every brand how many emails it sends a month. An answer of 8 or more sends Rollo a Slack message about a retainer. In October that was 6 of 19 inquiries. The other 13 went to his project list, sorted by deadline.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Copywriter Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a copywriter landing page that names your niche and turns a ready reader into a priced brief.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose samples that moved a number
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the one action a visitor takes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the client and the format in one sentence, such as onboarding emails for meal-kit brands. A prospect should know on the first read whether you write for people like them. A narrow line is easier to back with samples than a broad one.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the three pieces whose results a client is willing to share, and ask each client before you publish anything. Note the format and the metric next to every sample. A short set with results reads stronger than a long portfolio without them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what a ready reader does next, such as asking for a quote or booking a call. One action per page keeps the form short. Every section above the form should point toward that single request, including the samples and the prices.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a price per email, per page, or per month, whichever matches how you sell. A visible starting price tells a prospect early whether the budget fits. If a project cannot be priced up front, ask for a budget range in the form instead.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your positioning line, your samples, your prices, and the questions the form should ask into one prompt. Emergent drafts every section and sets up the inquiry table. Read the first draft on a phone screen, then fix by prompt anything that wraps badly.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill in the form as a prospect would, with a real deadline and a real budget. Check that the row lands in your table with every answer, and that the alert reaches you where you will see it. Fix confusing form wording now, before a client meets it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the first month of inquiries
fields.howto_step_7_des: After 30 days, count the inquiries by section and by project type. If one sample brings in the largest share of requests, move it higher on the page. If prospects keep asking something the page skips, answer it on the page.

plan.angle: The top 10 for a copywriter landing page splits between guides on writing landing page copy and agency pages selling copywriters for hire; none shows a copywriter how to build the page that sells their own writing. This page does: four copywriters' pages built from a prompt, each with the one mechanism that turns a reader into a paying brief (a free headline teardown, a per-email quote, a before-and-after case study with the client's numbers, and a retainer question that sorts inquiries), plus seven steps that start with the positioning line and end with reading the first month of inquiries.
